root_cause_analysis_sprint_6_4_commit_mi.mechanism_of_divergence: A Git commit SHA is a SHA-1/SHA-256 hash calculated over the commit object, which includes the tree hash (containing all file contents), parent commit hash, author name, committer name, and exact author/committer timestamps down to the second. Attempting to embed the prospective commit SHA inside a tracked file prior to running 'git commit' alters the content of the file, thereby changing the tree hash, which in turn alters the resulting commit SHA. This creates a circular self-referential paradox that is mathematically impossible to satisfy. Additionally, rebasing onto remote changes alters parent commit hashes, further guaranteeing divergent commit hashes.
root_cause_analysis_sprint_6_4_commit_mi.mathematical_impossibility: Commit SHA is a non-linear cryptographic function of its own contents.

stage_1_in_tree_manifest.scope: Tracks immutable content hashes of code, deliverables, tests, base commit, and environment

stage_2_detached_post_commit_attestation.scope: Attests to the exact Git commit SHA after 'git commit' is finalized
